title: Isoperimetric Lemma: the inductive bookkeeping behind "roughly" must be made quantitative

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
In the proof of Lemma `isoperimetriclemma` (general isoperimetric inequality, induction on $k$), case $V\ge c(n)R_1^k$ with $k>1$, the text writes:

> "If the volume of $z$ is equal to $c(n)R_1\cdots R_j\rho^{k-j}$ ... then the volume of $z_1$ is **roughly** $R_2\cdots R_j\rho^{(k-1)-(j-1)}$ for the same $\rho$."

The Federer-Fleming reduction $z'=[0,R_1]\times z_1$ only gives $\Vol(z_1)\le C(n)V/R_1$, i.e. control of $z_1$ up to a multiplicative constant. But the induction hypothesis applied to $z_1$ in the $(n-1)$-rectangle $[0,R_2]\times\cdots\times[0,R_n]$ requires writing
$$\Vol(z_1)=c(n-1)\,R_2\cdots R_{j'}\,\rho'^{\,(k-1)-j'}$$
with a **specific** pair $(j',\rho')$ satisfying $R_{j'}\le\rho'\le R_{j'+1}$.

**What must be proved:** that the constants $c(n),C(n)$ can be chosen (e.g. $c(n)=c(n-1)/C_{FF}$) so that
1. the slicing preserves the regime index, $j'=j-1$, and keeps $\rho'\sim\rho$ inside the correct interval $R_{j'}\le\rho'\le R_{j'+1}$;
2. the deformation cost $C(n)R_1(R_1\cdots R_j)\rho^{k-j}$ is absorbed into the target profile $C(n)R_1\cdots R_j\rho^{k-j+1}$ without breaking the inductive form.

This "roughly" hides the central quantitative claim of the whole lemma (preservation of the profile $(j,\rho)$ under slicing) and is currently an unjustified key step (gap type F3). A complete proof must track the constants explicitly through the induction.

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body: **Status (current revision):** the constant-tracking part is now fully addressed — Case 1/Case 2 are rewritten with explicit $C_{FF},c(n),C(n)$ bookkeeping and a dedicated 'Bookkeeping of constants' remark. However two precise residues remain, split off as new issues: (i) the *monotonicity* of the filling profile $I^{k-1}_{R'}(V)$ in $V$, needed to use the upper bound on $\Vol(z_1)$ — see prob-04-9; (ii) the structural claim $z'=[0,R_1]\times z_1$ (eq. prodform), still asserted — see prob-04-10.

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
## Mathematical Review (critic-agent, current `solution.tex` revision)

I re-reviewed the **current** expanded `solution.tex` against all open issues. Most previously-flagged gaps are now genuinely closed by the revision; a few residues remain; and I found **two new load-bearing gaps** filed as **prob-04-11** and **prob-04-12**. Full write-up linked as "Critic Analysis" (analysis.md).

### Closed by the current text
- **prob-04-2** (constant bookkeeping): explicit `cn-choice`,`cn-FF`, bookkeeping remark. ✔
- **prob-04-9** (monotonicity of $I^{k-1}_{R'}$): now Remark `rem:monotone`, stated and used. ✔ — *recommend resolving.*
- **prob-04-7** (coarea): derived via $p=(f_3,f_4)$, correct weight/direction. ✔
- **prob-04-6** (degree-1 restriction, $f_*h_{3,R}=h_{3,S}$): explicit intersection-number Steps 1–3; orientation identity (intersection sign $=\mathrm{sign}\det d_xf$) reconfirmed numerically (20000 random $M\in GL_4$, 0 mismatches). ✔
- **prob-04-8** (quantitative $\beta_1,F^*\omega_i$ bounds): written out; exponent algebra rechecked. ✔
- (resolved) **prob-04-10** product structure `prodform`: cellular Eilenberg–Zilber proof. ✔

### Residues still present
- **prob-04-3:** the convention $R_0:=0$ / empty product $:=1$ is *used* (Case 1 and `lemmaisoperimetric2` $j=0$ branch) but still not declared in the *statement* of `isoperimetriclemma`. One-line fix.
- **prob-04-5:** the model map $g_1$ with $L(g_1)=1$, $\mathrm{Dil}_1\lesssim1$, its scaling, and $\|\omega_i\|_\infty\lesssim S_1^{-2}$ remain **citation-only** (\cite{GH} Prop 5.2). The most substantial outstanding existence+quantitative claim.
- **prob-04-4:** the *piecewise-smooth* compactly-supported de Rham theorem is invoked without a precise citation. Low priority.

### NEW gaps (filed)
- **prob-04-11 — relative-cycle property of $f^{-1}(\Sigma_{a,b})$.** The proof treats $W=f^{-1}(\Sigma_{a,b})$ as a relative $2$-cycle in $(R,\partial R)$ (to build $h_{2,R}$ and to fill it by $z_3$, then apply `lemmaisoperimetric2`), but never proves $\partial[W]\subset\partial R$. The map-of-pairs hypothesis gives $f(\partial R)\subset\partial S$, **not** $f^{-1}(\partial S)\subset\partial R$; so $f^{-1}(\partial\Sigma_{a,b})\subset f^{-1}(\partial S)$ could be interior to $R$. Needs the standard transverse-preimage / Poincaré–Lefschetz lemma. (prob-04-6 only handles the *degree* of $f|_W$, assuming $W$ is already a relative cycle.)
- **prob-04-12 — well-definedness of $L_{h_{3,R}}(F)$ and legality of $\beta_1$.** Using the boundary-touching primitive $\beta_1$ to compute $L_{h_{3,R}}(F)$ is justified only by `lemmalink` item (2), whose hypothesis is that an interior-supported $\alpha_1$ exists for $F$ on $(R,\partial R\cup f^{-1}\Sigma)$, i.e. $F^*\Omega_i=0$ there. Neither $g^*\Omega_i=0$ (target pair) nor $F^*\Omega_i=f^*g^*\Omega_i=0$ (source pair) is ever stated. Functoriality fix, but currently absent and underwriting the central upper bound `stepSz`.

### Bottom line
The argument's skeleton is correct and the revision is strong. The remaining mathematically *substantive* items are: **prob-04-5** (self-contained model map) and the two new gaps **prob-04-11** (relative-cycle property — the deepest) and **prob-04-12** (definability/legality of the linking computation for $F$). The rest are one-line conventions.
